newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-Notionnel vol bolstered by poll, Fed fears.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Notionnel vol bolstered by poll, Fed fears.

text.p: Volatility of Notionnel options traded on the MATIF continued to rise as players hedged against a surprise left-wing lead in French elections on Sunday and uncertainty over U.S. rates, traders said on Thursday.

The July at-the-money Notionnel vol on September futures has gained 70 percentage points in the last 10 days to 5.50-5.80 percent and is trading 50 percentage points above September, brokers in Paris said.
"Vols are set to go up. It's true that the vol is expensive in July but it's going to be justified," said Jonathan Morris, options broker at Finacor in Paris.
"I think we are moving into a volatile period because of the elections and because the Fed did nothing now, leaving a lot of speculation about what they are going to do next time," he said.

A majority win for the ruling centre-right coalition in the first round of parliamentary elections on Sunday could weigh on options vols, traders said. But if the Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin emerged as a winner, vols should spike even higher as investors were likely to rush to sell the underlying Notionnel futures.
The second round of elections will be held on June 1.

Opinion polls published before last weekend's legal blackout suggested the combined left had drawn almost level with the ruling coalition in voting intentions, although all projected a reduced centre-right majority.
On Thursday, the vols on June at-the-money strikes on June Notionnel futures were trading at around 6.40 percent. September was flat at 5.05-5.15 volatility.
PIBOR options were trading at flat volatilities of between 33-38 percent in June and 21.5-24.5 percent on September, traders said.
Notionnel options came under a heavy selling assault on Wednesday when two U.S. firms sold about 20,000 June 130 straddles.
But some traders said at higher vols on Thursday, the deal, if played on the short side, was already showing a net loss.
"Hopefully they were closing positions because if they were taking one, they are losing money on it," said Morris.
Traders were looking at July as the ideal expiry to hold.
"It's not just gamma that you're getting long but there is a lot of vega there because it's a back month," Morris said.
Gamma is the measure of the rate of change in the delta of the underlying asset price. Vega is the rate of change of value of an option, compared with a change in volatility.
Traders also noted some put buying in recent days as an insurance against further falls in Notionnel.
Another trader said PIBOR-Euromark spread would shrink in the coming days from around minus 30 now. "If the right wins there is no reason for such a huge gap," said one trader.
